reference.lower_end_target: a 4-core Intel machine, ~3x slower than the M1 on this workload
reference.lower_end_status: ASSUMED — the operator has not named the target machine; every budget below is labelled with the factor it would need re-basing
reference.factor_note: the factor scales CPU-time budgets only; the data-volume budgets (bytes/frame, MB/s) are the wire volume and are machine-independent

allowances.ingest_note: per CONSUMED frame: our post-processing + encode (the live post segment, measured 1.18-1.68 ms in #112) plus the two untimed vendor calls' allowance (~5.6-6.4 ms, from #134's 9.6 ms residual less the platform's wait overshoot, #147 section 9)

budgets.derived_from: #147 section 5 measured 44.62 ms for a 41 ms request (zero work in the loop); this is the platform's own timer, so it caps the rate at ~22 Hz whatever the code does
#147 section 5 measured 24.29 ms for a 20 ms request; the ceiling for a 50 Hz pace
the same control at the 60 Hz pace (16 ms request); measured by this harness, not in #147
#136's live V1 frame: 20,000 points (kLiveBroadcastPointBudget) = 240,036 B; a change means a different point budget or a format change

the live post segment measured 1.18-1.68 ms at p50 in #112 covers decode + encode; the encoder alone is 533-546 us over six runs of this harness, so 800 us is ~1.5x the measured cost - a 2x regression trips it

#147 section 7: the encoder is 63% of the tick's CPU with no client, i.e. ~123 us of the 195 us tick, for the 2,304-point synthetic frame; this harness measures 61-85 us over six runs, so 120 us is ~1.4x the measured cost - a 2x regression trips it

#147 section 6 measured 35.9-38.4 us per client per tick at 8 clients (the tick's own condition, where the client drains in the background); this harness measures 17.6-22.6 us over six runs with a 4 MB receive buffer on its client, so 35 us is ~1.5x the measured cost - a 2x regression trips it

#147 section 6: the bcast segment was 0.29-0.31 ms per tick at 8 clients for the 27,697 B synthetic frame; this budget is for the 240,036 B live frame, measured 141-181 us over six runs, so 280 us is ~1.5x the measured cost - a 2x regression trips it

#147 section 3 measured the synthetic tick's post segment at 0.12-0.20 ms p50 (2,304 points, copy + rotate + encode); this harness measures 0.07-0.12 ms, so 0.20 ms is ~1.7x the measured cost - a 2x regression trips it

#147 section 3 measured the bcast segment at 0.10 ms p50 with one client; the harness runs the synthetic server with NO client, so this line is the no-client case (the broadcast is skipped) - the with-client cost is the bcast.* budgets above

#147 section 3.2 measured the live allocation footprint flat at 86-87 KB over 30 s (the tick allocates and frees every cycle); the harness reads the same malloc zone's ALLOCATED column from the running synthetic server

budget_rule: the CPU budgets are ~1.4-1.7x the cost measured over six runs of the harness, so a 2x regression trips them while the shared machine's noise does not; the platform's wait-floor budgets carry ~10% (they move with the machine's load) and the memory budget 1.3x
